settingsPanel.title: Settings
settingsPanel.subtitle: Devices, appearance, stream, and maintenance
settingsPanel.maintKeepHint: Keeps the last {days} days of logs/cache
settingsPanel.aboutTagline: A hub to connect, launch and control your Android tablets — USB, Wi‑Fi, mirroring and multi-session.
settingsPanel.aboutFeat1Desc: Live detection, renaming, colors, and Wi‑Fi ADB toggle. In mirroring, USB ↔ Wi‑Fi only updates the connection ID — the stream continues without interruption.
settingsPanel.aboutFeat2Desc: Launch an app on a virtual display (clones & profiles), with device/app picker and recents. A USB ↔ Wi‑Fi switch relaunches the session to reattach the display.
settingsPanel.aboutFeat3Desc: Controllable scrcpy stream with resolution, DPI, FPS, bitrate, GOP, and codec presets. In mirroring, USB ↔ Wi‑Fi stays seamless: only the connection ID is refreshed.
settingsPanel.aboutFeat4Desc: Show multiple sessions in grid, focus or duo, with an active tile for control.
settingsPanel.aboutFeat5Desc: Floating dock: screen, portrait, audio, Home. Batteries plus per-device Mute / Wi‑Fi during stream.
settingsPanel.aboutFeat6Desc: Classic rail or full-screen tablet UI (richer Home, dock). Set in Settings → Appearance, or from the Home screen.
settingsPanel.aboutFeat7Desc: Quickly find and relaunch recently used apps and profiles.
settingsPanel.aboutFeat8Desc: Shortcuts, step-by-step mirroring guide, Wi‑Fi setup, appearance, and built-in troubleshooting.
settingsPanel.aboutFeat9Desc: Clean logs, cache and history — manually or automatically on startup.
settingsPanel.aboutFeat10Desc: Check, download and install new versions from About.
settingsPanel.aboutFeat11Desc: Hub accent color, background moods (Midnight, Ocean, Dusk…), and a custom image via the Windows file picker. Preferences are remembered.
settingsPanel.accentLead: Accent for buttons, tabs, and active elements.

tips.resolution: Sets the video stream resolution. Higher values improve sharpness, at the cost of increased CPU load and bandwidth.
tips.fps: Frame rate of the stream. Higher values improve fluidity, but increase processor and network usage.
tips.dpi: Android display density. Lower values enlarge the interface; higher values make it more compact.
tips.bitrate: Stream bitrate (Mbps). Higher values improve image quality and require more bandwidth.
tips.gop: Interval between keyframes (I-frames). A shorter interval improves resilience to packet loss, with a slight bitrate overhead.
tips.videoCodec: Video compression codec. H.265 is more efficient; H.264 offers broader device compatibility.

wifi.title: Connect a device over WiFi
wifi.note: If the network or IP changes, reconnect with the toggle. In mirroring, USB ↔ Wi‑Fi only refreshes the connection ID (no dropout). For a virtual-display app, a link change relaunches the session.

steps.title: Plug in the device over USB
steps.lead: The first WiFi setup goes through USB to configure ADB.
steps: Connect your device via USB and make sure it is detected in the Hub.
USB debugging must be enabled on the phone.
Choose File transfer (MTP) if Android asks for the USB mode.
steps.tip: Without USB detection, the WiFi toggle cannot configure the device.

steps.title: Check the WiFi network
steps.lead: The phone and PC must be on the same local network.
steps: Connect the phone to WiFi.
Make sure this computer is on the same network (not an isolated guest network).
Avoid VPNs that isolate local traffic if the connection fails.
steps.tip: Guest networks often block device-to-device communication.

steps.title: Turn on the WiFi toggle
steps.lead: The Hub configures WiFi ADB and saves the device.
steps: Click the WiFi toggle next to the device in the sidebar.
On first connection, name the device when the Hub asks.
When ready, a Connected over WiFi message appears.
steps.tip: You can rename the device later in Settings → Devices.

steps.title: Unplug the USB cable
steps.lead: The device stays reachable while on the same WiFi.
steps: Unplug the USB cable — the WiFi session continues.
To switch back to USB, click the toggle again (settings stay saved).
Find USB and WiFi devices in Settings → Devices.
steps.tip: If the IP changes, reconnect with the WiFi toggle.

steps.title: Connect your phone
steps.lead: Use a USB data cable (not charge-only).
steps: Connect your Android phone to your computer via USB.
On the phone, choose File transfer (MTP) if Android asks for the USB mode.
Avoid cheap USB hubs — plug directly into the computer if possible.
steps.tip: If nothing happens when you plug in the cable, it is often a charge-only cable. Try the one that came with your phone.

steps.title: Enable developer options
steps.lead: This step is only required once per device.
steps: Open Settings → About phone.
Find Build number (or Version number).
Tap it 7 times until you see the You are now a developer message.
steps.tip: The exact label varies by brand (Samsung, Xiaomi, etc.) but the principle is the same.

steps.title: Enable USB debugging
steps.lead: Android Hub communicates with your phone via ADB — USB debugging is required.
steps: Go to Settings → System → Developer options.
Enable USB debugging.
On Xiaomi / Realme / Oppo: also allow USB debugging (Security settings) if offered.
steps.tip: On some brands, developer options are under Settings → Additional settings.

steps.title: Authorize the connection
steps.lead: Your phone will ask you to trust this computer.
steps: An Allow USB debugging? prompt appears on the phone.
Check Always allow from this computer.
Tap Allow.
steps.tip: If the prompt does not appear, unplug/replug the cable and unlock the phone screen.

steps.title: You're all set!
steps.lead: Your phone is now detected by Android Hub.
steps: The device appears in the Connected devices panel on the left.
Open New instance, select the device and an application — or click Mirroring to display the full screen.
Each session opens in a dedicated tab that you can control with the mouse and keyboard.
Enable Stream Deck mode to view multiple sessions (grid, focus, duo).
Tune resolution / DPI / FPS in Settings → Control (presets).
steps.tip: Pick Classic or New interface in Settings → Appearance. Double-click a recent item to relaunch an app.

appearance.title: Customize appearance
appearance.intro: Settings → Appearance centralizes interface style, accent color, background mood, and a custom image. Choices are saved and applied on the next launch.

sections.title: Classic or New interface
sections.body: Classic interface keeps the full side rail. New interface switches to a full-screen tablet layout: richer Home (connected devices, recent apps), floating dock, and lighter navigation. You can also switch from the Home screen.

sections.title: Hub color
sections.body: The accent colors active buttons, tabs, links, and indicators. Ten shades match the device color palette — text and badges stay readable.

sections.title: Hub background
sections.body: Eight dark moods (Midnight, Graphite, Slate, Forest, Ocean, Dusk, Wine, Cocoa) tint the backdrop without changing content. Ideal for a sober, consistent look.

sections.title: Custom image
sections.body: Choose an image… opens the Windows file picker (JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP). The image fills the Hub with a soft veil so labels stay readable. Remove restores color moods. Settings and Help windows always stay opaque.

troubleshoot.title: Quick troubleshooting
items: No device visible: check the USB cable (data, not charge-only) and MTP mode.
Allow USB debugging does not appear: unlock the screen and replug the cable.
Device disconnects randomly: plug directly into the PC and avoid USB hubs.
Mirroring does not start: close other ADB tools (Android Studio, scrcpy CLI).
Keyboard input ignored: click once on the video stream to focus it.
AZERTY keyboard: accented letters, Shift (digits and ?./§%…), Alt Gr (@, #, {, }), and € are sent to the device. Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch session tabs (not typing).
Empty Stream Deck mode: start at least one session (mirroring or instance) from Connected devices or New instance.
Incomplete Duo mode: open the Duo menu (Duo button) and pick Device 1 and Device 2 from the list.
Wi‑Fi fails: same network as the PC, Wi‑Fi on on the phone, avoid VPN / guest networks.
IP not found on Wi‑Fi toggle: enable phone Wi‑Fi then try again.
No battery on the dock: the device must be connected (USB or Wi‑Fi) and visible in Connected devices.
Scroll zoom does nothing: click the video stream once to focus it.
Mirroring USB↔Wi‑Fi: the stream should not drop (only the ID changes). App instance: a brief session refresh is normal to reattach the display.
